trial_court: JMFC, Jabalpur (Criminal Complaint Case Pr No.181/2015)
case_name: Shekhar Nigam vs Smt. Ekta Nigam
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner's marriage with respondent was solemnised on 20.11.2009. Respondent lodged a criminal complaint under Section 498-A of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act on 17.07.2012. Petitioner filed a petition for divorce under C Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act. Respondent also lodged an application under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C. on 06.02.2013.

legal_principles.principle: A wife who is leading an adulterous life has no right to maintenance.
legal_principles.held: Though the divorced wife is also entitled for maintenance till she enters into a second marriage, but a wife who is leading an adulterous life, has no right to maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: The principle of granting maintenance to the non-applicant wife is guided by the same principles provided under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C.
legal_principles.held: If the Magistrate is satisfied that the application prima facie discloses that the husband is committing or has committed the act of domestic violence or there is likelihood that the husband may commit an act of domestic violence, he may grant an ex parte order on the basis of affidavit as may be prescribed in such form.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act

legal_principles.principle: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 does not create any additional right to claim maintenance on the part of the aggrieved person.
legal_principles.held: It only puts the enforcement of existing right of maintenance available to an aggrieved person on fast track.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
cited_cases: Rachna Kathuria v. Ramesh Kathuria, (2010) X SCC Y

outcome.final_order: Order dated 13.07.2015 passed in Criminal Complaint Case Pr No.181/2015 is quashed and consequential proceeding is set aside.
